quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #21
										  					
  

40 Questions • Passing Score 32

questions.question: On most roadways, you should signal ____ before you turn.
questions.explanation: Use your turn signal to warn other drivers before you turn or change lanes. On most roads, signal at least 100 feet before turning. On highways, signal at least 500 feet before turning.

questions.question: Your body gets rid of about:
questions.explanation: The average person's body processes about one drink per hour. How impaired you become depends on many things: how much you drink, how fast you drink it, your body weight, whether you have eaten, and your overall health.

questions.question: When passing another vehicle on a two-lane road with traffic in opposite directions, you should:

options.text: Return to the right lane when there is enough space between you and the vehicle you passed.
Stay in the left lane if you plan to turn left.
Return to the right side of the road immediately.

questions.correctAnswerText: Return to the right lane when there is enough space between you and the vehicle you passed.
questions.explanation: After passing another vehicle on a two-lane road, return to the right lane as soon as there is enough space between you and the vehicle you just passed.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: Fines double in a work zone.

questions.explanation: Warning signs tell drivers about upcoming road conditions and hazards. They are usually yellow with black markings. This sign warns you that cyclists may cross the road.

questions.question: On a highway, you should signal ____ before you turn.
questions.explanation: Use your turn signal to warn other drivers before you turn or change lanes. On highways, signal at least 500 feet before turning.

questions.question: When exiting a highway, you should start slowing down:

options.text: On the main road, just before the exit lane.
Once you see a toll booth.
After you move into the exit lane.
When you first see the exit sign.

questions.correctAnswerText: After you move into the exit lane.
questions.explanation: Move into the exit lane early. Do not slow down until after you are in the exit lane.

questions.question: Driving faster:

options.text: Makes it easier to see cross traffic.
Has no effect on your field of vision.

questions.explanation: The faster you drive, the smaller your field of vision becomes. As you go faster, you see less of what's around you. Stay alert to hazards.

questions.question: When driving in fog, use:

options.text: It does not matter which lights you use.

questions.explanation: Use low beam headlights when driving in fog, rain, or snow.

questions.question: When driving past a vehicle that just parked on the side of the road, you should:

options.text: Be ready for the driver to open the car door.
Assume the driver will wait for you to pass before opening the door.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be ready for the driver to open the car door.
questions.explanation: When passing a vehicle that just parked, be prepared for the driver to open the door. Use extra caution when driving near parked vehicles.

questions.question: You must not drive faster than:

options.text: A speed that is reasonable and safe.
A speed that is safe for the current conditions.

questions.explanation: Never drive faster than is reasonable and safe. Match your speed to the area, traffic, pedestrians, weather, road quality, and light. Always obey legal speed limits.

questions.question: You are waiting in the intersection to turn left. What should you do?

options.text: Signal and turn your wheels to the left.
Signal and keep your wheels straight.
Flash your headlights to get other drivers to let you through.
Drive around the back of a car that blocks you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Signal and keep your wheels straight.
questions.explanation: Always signal before turning. Keep your wheels straight while waiting to turn left. If another car hits you from behind, straight wheels keep you from being pushed into oncoming traffic.

questions.question: A solid white line on the right edge of the road angles left toward the center. What does this mean?

options.text: You are approaching a construction area.

questions.explanation: A solid line on the side of the road marks the edge. When the line angles toward the center, the road is getting narrower ahead.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that a flagger is controlling traffic in a construction area ahead.

questions.question: When must you yield to other drivers?

options.text: When entering a street from a garage or alley.
When a car on your left reaches an unmarked intersection at the same time as you.
When your traffic signal is a green arrow.

questions.correctAnswerText: When entering a street from a garage or alley.
questions.explanation: You must yield when entering from an alley, driveway, or garage. You must also yield to pedestrians crossing on an intersecting sidewalk.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: Eight-sided signs mean stop. You must stop and give the right-of-way to other traffic. You may go when it is safe.

questions.question: When turning right on a green light, you must:

options.text: Stop and look for police cars.

questions.explanation: You may turn right or left at a green light (unless a sign says not to). When you turn, you must yield to other vehicles and pedestrians in the intersection.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: The road curves right ahead. Slow down to 35 mph.
A divided highway begins. Slow down to 35 mph.
Merge ahead. Slow down to 35 mph.
Winding road ahead. Slow down to 35 mph.

questions.correctAnswerText: The road curves right ahead. Slow down to 35 mph.
questions.explanation: This sign warns that the road curves to the right. Slow down to the safe speed shown on the sign, which is 35 mph.

questions.question: Your car hits a parked car and you cannot find the owner. What must you do?

options.text: Leave a written note with your name, address, and what happened.

questions.correctAnswerText: Leave a written note with your name, address, and what happened.
questions.explanation: Stop and try to find the owner. If you cannot, leave a written note with your name, address, and details of the accident.

questions.question: You want to turn left at a green light, but traffic is heavy. What should you do?

options.text: Wait at the crosswalk for traffic to clear.
Wait in the center of the intersection for traffic to clear.
Go because you have a green light.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait in the center of the intersection for traffic to clear.
questions.explanation: Wait for oncoming traffic to pass before turning left. If the light is green and no car ahead is turning left, you may enter the intersection to prepare for your turn.

questions.question: A flashing yellow light at an intersection means:

options.text: Slow down and proceed with care.
Stop until a green light appears.
Stop until the way is clear.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and proceed with care.
questions.explanation: A flashing yellow light means caution. Slow down, look both ways, and proceed carefully.

questions.question: At a yield sign, what should you do?

options.text: Always stop before entering the intersection.
Yield only to traffic on the right.
Yield only to traffic on the left.
Slow down and let other traffic go first.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and let other traffic go first.
questions.explanation: A yield sign means you must slow down and let traffic in the intersection go first before you enter.

questions.question: You cannot park within ____ of a fire hydrant.
questions.explanation: You cannot park within 15 feet of a fire hydrant. Park in legal spots where other drivers can see your vehicle from both directions.

questions.question: What does a solid white line down the center of a two-lane road mean?

options.text: Traffic moves in opposite directions and you cannot pass.
Traffic moves in opposite directions and you can pass when safe.
Traffic moves in the same direction and you cannot pass.
Traffic moves in the same direction and you can pass when safe.

questions.correctAnswerText: Traffic moves in the same direction and you cannot pass.
questions.explanation: White lines separate traffic moving in the same direction. A solid white line means you cannot pass.

questions.question: When can you cross a solid yellow line?

options.text: To pass traffic moving in the same direction.

questions.explanation: You can cross broken lines, but not solid lines. You can only cross a solid yellow line when turning.

questions.question: When should you use hand-over-hand steering?

options.text: When backing up or using your blinkers, radio, or wipers.

questions.explanation: Use hand-over-hand steering when turning slowly, like at an intersection or when parking. Position your left hand between 8 and 9 o'clock and your right hand between 3 and 4 o'clock on the wheel.

questions.question: When visibility is poor, what should you do first?
questions.explanation: Slowing down is your first response to poor visibility and dangerous road conditions.

questions.question: What does a double solid yellow line down the center of a two-lane road mean?

options.text: Traffic moves in opposite directions and you cannot pass.
Traffic moves in opposite directions and you can pass when safe.
Traffic moves in the same direction and you cannot pass.
Traffic moves in the same direction and you can pass when safe.

questions.correctAnswerText: Traffic moves in opposite directions and you cannot pass.
questions.explanation: Yellow lines separate traffic moving in opposite directions. A solid yellow line means you cannot pass.

questions.question: At an intersection with a flashing red light, you must:

options.text: Slow down and drive carefully through.
Turn right or left because the road ahead is blocked.
Stop and wait for a flashing green light.
Stop, then go when it is safe.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop, then go when it is safe.
questions.explanation: A flashing red light means you must come to a complete stop. Then proceed when the way is clear.

questions.question: When driving near children at play, you should expect them to:

options.text: Know when it is safe to cross the street.
Stop at the curb before crossing.
Run in front of you without looking.

questions.correctAnswerText: Run in front of you without looking.
questions.explanation: Always slow down near children. They may not understand danger and could run in front of your car without looking.

questions.question: In normal weather and traffic, what is the minimum safe distance to stay behind another car?
questions.explanation: Keep at least four seconds of distance between your car and the car ahead during normal conditions. This gives you time to react. Increase this distance in bad weather or heavy traffic.

questions.question: When a bus is signaling to return to the main road after stopping, you must:

options.text: Honk to let them know you are there.

questions.explanation: You must yield to any bus that is signaling to return to the main road after loading or unloading passengers. Slow down, change lanes, or stop to let the bus safely merge into traffic.

questions.question: Roads freeze quickly when they are:
questions.explanation: In cold or wet weather, roads in shade freeze faster. Areas under trees or buildings freeze before the rest of the road and are the last to dry.

questions.question: When you see or hear an emergency vehicle coming, you should:

options.text: Stop immediately and let the vehicle pass.
Move to the right side of the road as safely as possible and stop.
Drive slowly and let the vehicle pass.
Keep moving slowly, staying to the right side of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move to the right side of the road as safely as possible and stop.
questions.explanation: You must yield to an emergency vehicle using lights or a siren. Move as far right as you safely can and stop. Do not stop in an intersection.

questions.question: At a stop sign, you should stop and:

options.text: Check your rearview mirror for tailgating cars.
Move when the vehicle ahead moves.
Look right, then left, then right again.
Look left, then right, then left again.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look left, then right, then left again.
questions.explanation: Look left first because vehicles from the left are closer to you. Then look right, then look left again to catch any traffic you may have missed.

questions.question: Blood alcohol content (BAC) depends on each of the following, except:

options.text: How much time passes between drinks.

questions.explanation: Blood alcohol content depends on how much you drink, how much time passes between drinks, and your weight. Physical fitness does not affect BAC.

questions.question: A speed limit is:

options.text: The maximum or minimum legal speed on a road in dangerous conditions.
The maximum or minimum legal speed on a road in ideal conditions.
The suggested speed on a road in ideal conditions.

questions.correctAnswerText: The maximum or minimum legal speed on a road in ideal conditions.
questions.explanation: A speed limit is the maximum or minimum legal speed under ideal conditions. You may drive slower, but not faster. Slow down in school zones, work zones, and bad weather.

questions.question: In a school zone, the speed limit is ____ the posted speed limit.
questions.explanation: In a school zone, the speed limit is 10 mph below the posted limit. This applies 45 minutes before school starts until school ends, and for 45 minutes after school closes. Always drive carefully in school zones.

questions.question: When merging onto a freeway, it is usually best to:

options.text: Drive slowly while waiting for an opening.
Turn on your hazard lights until safely on the freeway.
Speed up to match freeway traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Speed up to match freeway traffic.
questions.explanation: Use the on-ramp to speed up to match freeway traffic so you can blend in smoothly and safely. Merging traffic must yield to traffic already on the freeway.

questions.question: Signs for public recreation areas are:
questions.explanation: Brown signs point to cultural, historical, and recreation areas. They help you find places of interest when traveling.

questions.question: If you need to stop quickly and your vehicle does not have Anti-Lock Brakes (ABS), you should:
questions.explanation: Pumping your brakes is the best way to stop quickly in an emergency. This lets you stop fast while keeping control of the steering.
